title: Embedding onboarding smoke tests and rerank traffic-shaping mitigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a lightweight, reproducible smoke-test and traffic-shaping guardrail to the embedding and reranking onboarding flow. Goal: avoid quality regressions and cost/latency spikes when new embedding models or reranker variants are introduced. This ticket covers: 1) a small deterministic smoke-suite that runs against each candidate model before rollout (latency, recall@k on a golden prompt set, token cost), 2) a traffic-shaping policy to throttle staged traffic and protect downstream rerank resources, and 3) automated telemetry checks that gate canary promotion. This is targeted at hosted + dedicated lanes and should surface clear pass/fail signals for PMs and Engs before increasing traffic beyond 5%.
acceptance_criteria: A smoke-test pipeline runs automatically for each embedding model candidate and produces a pass/fail signal within 10 minutes of model upload
Smoke tests include latency (p50/p95), a small recall@10/recall@100 on the curated golden set, and token cost estimation
A traffic-shaping policy in the gateway enforces staged ramps (0 -> 1% -> 5% -> 20%) with automatic rollback on telemetry failures
Dashboards updated: per-model smoke-test results, canary SLI panel, and a rerank-cost spike detector with alerting
Documentation page (Confluence) describing the smoke checks and ops playbook for failed rollouts

decisions: Use a small curated golden set (~500 queries) owned by PMs for smoke recall checks instead of attempting full-scale evals during rollout
Run smoke-suite in a short-lived CI job that executes model shard on one GPU to get realistic latency signals; do not run full production throughput tests
Traffic-shaper will be implemented as a policy in the adaptive gateway with percent-based ramp and time windows; we will not block by default but will auto-rollback on SLI thresholds
tradeoffs: Pros of small smoke-suite: fast feedback and low cost. Cons: may miss edge-case semantic regressions only visible at scale.
Using gateway traffic-shaping avoids changes to downstream services, but adds routing complexity and requires careful testing of percent-weighted routing correctness.
Priming KV cache in smoke test increases test runtime and flakiness risk but reduced production-first-request latency spikes observed in the spike.
tests: Smoke test job (CI) steps: upload candidate model -> run 500 golden queries -> collect p50/p95 latency, recall@10/100, token cost -> compute pass/fail against thresholds
Stress test: run 20 QPS for 10 minutes in staging to validate no downstream queue buildup for rerankers
Failure-mode test: simulate reranker OOM on staging and verify auto-rollback reduces canary traffic to 0% within 60s
rollout_plan: Shadow traffic for 24h (all requests duplicated to new model but not served responses)
Canary phase 1: route 1% traffic for 4 hours; monitor latency, recall delta, and cost delta
Canary phase 2: increase to 5% for 12 hours if no failing alerts
Gradual ramp to 20% over 48 hours; require manual approval to go to 100%
Automatic rollback triggers: p95 latency increase > 30% or recall@10 drop > 2% absolute or cost per 1k tokens > 20% increase
telemetry: New dashboard: embeddings/smoke_tests showing candidate runs, pass/fail, and historical baselines
Per-model SLI panel: p50/p95 latency, recall@k, tokens-per-request, reranker queue length
Tag smoke-test runs with model_hash and commit SHA for traceability
estimated_cost_change: small increase in CI minutes for smoke-suite (~$0.05 per candidate) and minor runtime overhead for gateway traffic-shaper
owner_notes: If smoke-suite shows marginal failures (near-threshold), create a label 'needs-eval' and trigger a human review by model-owner PM
Coordinate with reranker team to add per-call cost-tagging to attribution pipeline (dependency ENG-75290), otherwise cost alerts will be noisy
